items.title: Charles Elgar Interview, 1958-05-27
items.q: there was a Mrs. Bimford who was a welfare worker

ctx.x: That's good. See if there's any more questions here about these early days. It's mostly the early days that we're asking about because a lot of the later things we could read in the newspapers and the magazines and downbeat. Yeah. Back before they had a downbeat for instance.

Well, I went in with Patty with five pieces. That's when the craze of Dixonland music had just begun to hit Chicago. And I went to see him and ask him if he'd give me a chance with this outfit. At that time he had an 18 piece white orchestra. Frank Cavallo had the orchestra there. And he kind of hesitated for a minute because he didn't know how people would go for it. And I was fortunate enough to sell him on the idea of giving it a trial, which he agreed to do. Well, we went in there with the understanding that…
Rough. Who was in the band, do you remember?
